provedSourceFacts: Claim validates/authenticates first, then guidedRevoked completes its own REQUIRED transaction before main claim starts another REQUIRED repository transaction.

Both acquire the same session owner row; first SELECT state/revoked_at FOR UPDATE, second SELECT document/progress FOR UPDATE. SessionConfiguration and sweep use same unqualified PlatformTransactionManager; no custom propagation.

Between first commit and second acquisition, another same-owner model/observe/consume transaction can interpose. Existing sampler demonstrates contention at first acquisition but exact holder/dominance unobserved.
Revocation precheck can mutate revoked_at and LIVE_RECHECK audit and invokes installed guidedStop inside its transaction. Current caller throws SECRET_USE_REVOKED only AFTER that transaction commits.
nonEquivalentNaiveChange: Moving precheck inside main lambda then throwing would roll back real revocation/audit/stop effects; forbidden.
smallestPotentialCompositionForArchitect: An outer same REQUIRED transaction could contain unchanged existing guidedRevoked plus unchanged existing main transaction lambda, returning a private revoked-or-response decision. Revoked decision must exit normally to commit before identical public exception is thrown outside; nonrevoked original body/guards/return/clock/calls remain unchanged. This removes the owner release/reacquire interposition window without data/auth cache or skipped validation. No author release proposed from this report.
